description: The measured Scaffy W6 benchmark: five real Barkpark chores, four arms, 32 registered cells at pin 591fdcd53. The catalog-armed agent matches the raw engine byte-for-byte on every fully-covered chore; the engine does it for $0 in seconds with zero variance — and the paper reports every place the win narrows or the measurement has limits: the ~$0.55 spawn floor, the partial-coverage tax, the boundary staging leak, and predictions P1–P5 scored against the prereg.

blocks.caption: The three measured regimes. Full coverage: the engine wins outright. Partial: run it, then top up — and close the gap. None: agent work, and honestly no tax for having the catalog around.

content.value: A dollars-honesty note: at today's chore sizes the dollar column is the

argument for the engine — the ~$0.55 cache-dominated spawn floor means agent-vs-agent dollar gaps on small chores are noise. The strong, always-on arguments are the ones agents cannot buy at any spend: variance 0, seconds instead of minutes, and a remove that replays a receipt instead of hoping a hand-edit was clean. The engine does not beat the floor; it bypasses it.

. Engine scaffold: dry-run 9 ms, tokens 0 (real-run wall of 21–36 s was the ASSERT CMD gates, reported separately per D83). Growing the starters into real renderers was metered agent work: Go surface 426 s wall (merged, #3967); web surfaces 952 s (stamped in the task ledger, in review at publish time). That split is the crossover, lived: the deterministic slice takes milliseconds and zero tokens; judgment work stays agent work. This paper renders its diffs and file trees as plain code blocks — the web growth had not merged at publish time, and the honest choice was not to demo blocks the reader's surface cannot yet render.
